name: Color and pixel depth
plain: Bits per pixel the screen reports; almost always 24.
meaning: Reported colorDepth is 24 on nearly everything (30 on some wide-gamut Safari setups, 16 or 32 rarely). Low entropy but included in every library.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can see how many colors your screen reports, almost always 24 bit
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads.
can: Check the color depth number your screen reports
Pick image or video quality to match
Add the number to a browser fingerprint
cannot: Tell which monitor model you have
See your color profile or calibration
Learn much that is unique, since nearly every screen says 24

story.what_it_is: How many bits of color each screen pixel uses. It is almost always 24.

marketing.name: Screen.colorDepth
marketing.pitch: Documents a read only value that reports the number of bits used to show one color on the screen.

story.for_you: You never see this. The page just reads a number from your screen. On almost every device it says 24, so it changes nothing for you.
story.for_makers: Because nearly everyone reports 24, the value tells a site very little. Makers still read it to pick image formats. Fraud teams use odd values to spot fake browsers.

use_cases.example: A WebGL game picks the texture setup that fits the screen so colors in fog and fire do not band.
A dashboard counts how many visitors have unusual displays so designers know what to test.
A fraud service sees a browser that claims a depth no real screen reports and flags it as a possible bot.
A photo editor in the browser warns that the screen cannot show all the colors of a file.
An ad network adds the number to a device profile as one small clue among many.
A video player decides whether to offer richer color streams.

linkedin.how: Collected as color depth and pixel depth. Read by the LinkedIn APFC fingerprint script (alleged by BrowserGate, partly confirmed by BleepingComputer).
